options.content:
**Target** selects target storage, CPU, PCIe, and Falcon telemetry. Initiator and LMCache panels always show **mmgi0–mmgi5**. **Exported namespaces** reports active kernel NVMe-oF exports; zero means this target has none. Device filters only exported namespaces.

**`operation`** is the phase: `Load` is retrieve (reads), `Store` is insert (writes). The names appear on the **LMCache** tile above.

In a `Load`-only window **NVMe WR** and **RDMA RD** read ~0 by construction - that is the read path confirming itself, not a dead query. **LMCache**, **NVMe RD**, and **RDMA WR** carry the same read-response payload at successive stages; brief warmup-to-measured transitions can still differ.

**RDMA WR = target-side ULP-to-fabric TX**, the target response path; **RDMA RD = target-side fabric-to-ULP RX**. Live tiles use a 30s rate from scrape-time gRPC reads; Prometheus scrapes every 4s. The Falcon history chart uses the Grafana rate window. A failed ACC collection hides the affected target payload total.

panels.title: Reading this section

panels.description: Application payload goodput reported by the running bench l2 processes on the mmg initiators. The measured-phase series starts with the phase, so its rate reads low until the rate window fills; do not average the whole plotted curve for a 60s phase. Use the end-of-run JSON and counter gate for publishable throughput; this panel aligns the workload with the target-side host and NVMe trends.
panels.title: LMCache aggregate goodput (bits/s)

panels.description: Total application payload goodput per initiator process. The Prometheus endpoint is short-lived and exists only while bench l2 is running. The measured-phase series starts with the phase, so its rate reads low until the rate window fills. Operations are summed here to expose imbalance across mmgi0-mmgi5 without combining the read and write aggregate lines.
panels.title: LMCache goodput by initiator (bits/s)

panels.description: Current measured-phase completed-submit rate from the short-lived bench l2 Prometheus endpoints. The series is absent during warmup and after the run.
panels.title: LMCache completed submits/s (last 30s)

panels.description: Mean measured-phase submit-to-completion latency over the query window from the short-lived bench l2 Prometheus endpoints. The series is absent during warmup and after the run. The endpoint does not expose live percentiles; use the final benchmark summary for p50/p99.

targets.expr: sum by (operation) (rate(lmcache_bench_l2_submit_latency_seconds_total{job="lmcache_bench_6x2",host=~"mmgi.*",phase="measured"}[30s]) and on (host, initiator) (up{job="lmcache_bench_6x2",host=~"mmgi.*"} == 1)) / sum by (operation) (rate(lmcache_bench_l2_completed_submits_total{job="lmcache_bench_6x2",host=~"mmgi.*",phase="measured"}[30s]) and on (host, initiator) (up{job="lmcache_bench_6x2",host=~"mmgi.*"} == 1))

panels.title: LMCache mean submit latency by operation (last 30s)

panels.description: Configured in-flight target reported by each short-lived bench l2 Prometheus endpoint while the run is active.

targets.expr: max by (host, initiator) (lmcache_bench_l2_in_flight_target{job="lmcache_bench_6x2",host=~"mmgi.*",phase="measured"} and on (host, initiator) (up{job="lmcache_bench_6x2",host=~"mmgi.*"} == 1))

panels.title: LMCache configured in-flight submits per initiator
LMCache run details — submits · latency · in-flight

panels.description: Number of active exported namespaces per selected target. Zero means this target has no active kernel NVMe-oF namespace exports.

targets.expr: count by (host) (nvme_namespace_role{host=~"${target:regex}",role="exported"}) or on (host) (0 * max by (host) (up{job="node_6x2",host=~"${target:regex}"} == 1))

panels.title: Exported namespaces

panels.description: Aggregate kernel read throughput across the target physical namespaces selected by $device, in bits/s. The summary row carries the same figure in bits/s for comparison against the fabric ceiling. Do not add this target-media view to initiator md0: they observe the same traffic at different layers.
panels.title: NVMe read throughput (bits/s)

panels.description: Aggregate kernel write throughput across the target physical namespaces selected by $device, in bits/s. The summary row carries the same figure in bits/s for comparison against the fabric ceiling. Do not add this target-media view to initiator md0: they observe the same traffic at different layers.
panels.title: NVMe write throughput (bits/s)

panels.description: Kernel read throughput of each initiator RAID0 md0 device, in bits/s. Each md0 stripes eight private NVMe-oF namespaces. This is an initiator-layer view of the same I/O as target physical NVMe, so compare it for reconciliation but do not add the two.
panels.title: Initiator md0 read throughput (bits/s)

panels.description: Kernel write throughput of each initiator RAID0 md0 device, in bits/s. Each md0 stripes eight private NVMe-oF namespaces. This is an initiator-layer view of the same I/O as target physical NVMe, so compare it for reconciliation but do not add the two.
panels.title: Initiator md0 write throughput (bits/s)

panels.description: Kernel read throughput per drive, in bytes/s, on the same base as the aggregate above. Each drive keeps one colour across every per-drive and NVMe panel.
panels.title: Per-drive read throughput (bits/s)

panels.description: Kernel write throughput per drive, in bytes/s, on the same base as the aggregate above. Each drive keeps one colour across every per-drive and NVMe panel.
panels.title: Per-drive write throughput (bits/s)

panels.description: Kernel disk I/O active fraction. A value of 1.0 does not prove NVMe throughput saturation on a multi-queue device.
panels.title: Per-drive I/O active fraction

panels.description: Fraction of wall-clock time the controller reported itself busy, from SMART controller_busy_time. The counter has minute-level granularity, so short bursts are smeared.
panels.title: NVMe controller busy fraction

panels.description: Composite temperature from SMART, converted from Kelvin. Read it for throttling correlation rather than for absolute values.
panels.title: NVMe temperature

panels.description: SMART media_errors and num_err_log_entries, cumulative since power-on. A non-zero slope during a run is worth investigating; a flat non-zero value is history.
panels.title: NVMe error counters

panels.description: PCM event classification per direction and socket, on the same >1 GB/s traffic gate as the hit % panel beside it. Log y-axis because the miss series runs two to three orders of magnitude below the hit series and is invisible on a linear scale. Not an end-to-end DDIO proof.
panels.title: PCIe LLC hit/miss — all sockets (bytes/s, log)

panels.description: PCM hit / (hit + miss) per selected target, direction, and socket. Hidden below 1 GB/s of PCIe traffic to avoid idle-noise ratios. PCM cache classification is not end-to-end DDIO proof.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (host, direction, socket) (pcm_pcie_bandwidth_bytes_per_second{host=~"${target:regex}",classification="hit"}) / sum by (host, direction, socket) (pcm_pcie_bandwidth_bytes_per_second{host=~"${target:regex}",classification=~"hit|miss"}) and on (host, direction, socket) (pcm_pcie_bandwidth_bytes_per_second{host=~"${target:regex}",classification="total"} > 1e9)
